sentences: MUBUF `buffer_load*`, `buffer_store*`, and `buffer_atomic*` enforce `num_records` (V# word 2).
Out-of-bounds stores/atomics skip memory access completely and out-of-bounds loads return 0 without a load.

**The RX 6800 measurement behind RAW loads** (`buffer_load_dword`/`x2`/`x3`/`x4`, stride 0, no `idxen`, OOB_SELECT 3; the per-mode rule below covers every mode, stride and `idxen`): the byte offset O = inst_offset + soffset + (offen ? vaddr : 0) is exact (nothing truncated, and the address keeps base & 3), and dword i is data when O + 4·i + 4 ≤ num_records, else 0, measured on AMD Radeon RX 6800 (gfx1030, Windows driver 32.0.21045.29003) by running the instructions as a raw compute kernel, wave32 and wave64 (155 runs, every result either 0 or the stored data, wave32 = wave64 in every dword), for x1/x2/x4 with V# word3 0x31016fac (OOB_SELECT 3) at offsets 0..63 per lane, NUM_RECORDS 17..23 and 0x1000, base & 3 = 0 and 3: a dword at 0xf with NUM_RECORDS 18 is 0 (a start-only check reads it); x4 at 3 with 18 gives three data dwords and 0 for the fourth, which starts at 15 < 18 (so neither a whole-load nor a per-dword start check), and the zero is a whole 0, not partial bytes; x4 at offset:13 with 20 gives data, 0, 0, 0; inst_offset, soffset and offen are summed before the check; base & 3 = 3 flips at the same offsets.
`x3` gets the rule without a measurement.

**Per-mode check (V# OOB_SELECT, word3 bits [29:28])**, for every MUBUF/MTBUF access, as measured natively on RDNA2 (gfx1036, 732 cases, `docs/buffer_bounds.md`; Mesa's GFX11 column, not its GFX10 one).
`idx` = `vindex` (0 without `idxen`), `off` = inst_offset + vaddr offset (offen), `offs` = `off` + soffset.

A dword at byte 4·k of the access is out of range when: **0 STRUCTURED_WITH_OFFSET** `idx >= num_records` or `off + 4k + 4 > stride`; **1 STRUCTURED** `idx >= num_records` (no `idxen`: idx 0, so only `num_records == 0`); **2 DISABLED** `num_records == 0`; **3 RAW** `offs + 4k + 4 > num_records` (`idx * stride` is in the address, not in the check).
A literal word3 (`s_mov_b32` earlier in the block) folds the mode, a run-time one selects with `OpSelect`.

Multi-dword accesses, measured on the Radeon 880M (gfx1150, a valid proxy: gfx1036 follows the same column and gfx1150 matched it bit-exactly): in modes 0 and 3 **`buffer_load_dwordx2..x4` and `buffer_store_dwordx2..x4` are per dword**, for loads and stores alike (x4 at off 20 of 32 in RAW loads/stores 3 dwords, at 28 one, at 32 none; mode 0 likewise at the stride); modes 1 and 2 check once and always take the whole access.

**A typed element (`buffer_load_format_*`, `buffer_store_format_*`) is all or nothing and ends at its format's size** (32_32_32_32 at off 20 of 32 reads or writes nothing), and an atomic checks its dword's end like a dword access.

The translator does the same: per-dword guarded loads and stores for modes 0 and 3 (a store that straddled the edge used to write past it), the element size from the instruction's format, a literal word3 or the V#.

The same oracle confirmed the terms (504 `buffer_load_dword` probes, idxen/offen/inst_offset/soffset at the stride and record edges, 0 disagreements): mode 0's `off` has `inst_offset` and no soffset, mode 1 reads nothing but the index, mode 3 adds inst_offset and soffset.
`s_buffer_load` (SMEM) is separate: it keeps the `num_records` bound of the Scalar/buffer row and ignores OOB_SELECT (the same pattern for 0 to 3).

**Swizzle**: SWIZZLE_ENABLE (V# word1 bit 31, Mesa `gfx10-rsrc.json` line 326; word1 [31:30] on GFX11, `gfx11-rsrc.json` line 259) and ADD_TID_ENABLE (word3 bit 23, line 337) change the address and the bounds in every mode and are modelled; see the Swizzled buffer addressing row.
SWIZZLE_ENABLE and ADD_TID_ENABLE are modelled; see the Swizzled buffer addressing row.

SWIZZLE_ENABLE (V# word1 bit 31, Mesa `gfx10-rsrc.json` line 326; word1 [31:30] on GFX11, `gfx11-rsrc.json` line 259) and ADD_TID_ENABLE (word3 bit 23, line 337) change the address and the bounds in every mode and are not modelled: a literal V# with either set is `Unsupported`, a run-time V# with them is translated unswizzled, which is silently wrong (known gap).

Until 2026-11-22 the translator ignored OOB_SELECT and checked by stride alone (`offset < num_records`, `index < num_records`, or `offset < num_records * stride`): a V# with word3 = 0 (mode 0, stride 0) was fully readable and is now always out of range, as on hardware, so the test harnesses' output V# is `0x31016fac` now (`vk_compute_test`, the interpreter tests, `cs_bounds.asm`, `cs_fmt_1010102.asm`, `cs_store.asm`).

**How confirmed**: the native RDNA2 measurement (gfx1036) and the gfx1150 oracle (RDNA3.5, same column); GPU test `cs_oob_select.asm` (every mode, literal and run-time V#, words derived from the rules) on an NVIDIA RTX 5070 and an AMD Radeon 880M, which checks the translation, not RDNA2; `tests/semantic/test_buffer_oob_select.py` (a hand-written table of 33 cases over the four modes, loads and stores, both V# forms, plus the multi-dword stores and typed elements); `cs_oob_tail.asm` pins the end-based edge, per-dword x4 loads and stores and the all-or-nothing element, where Mesa's GFX10 column gives other words.

**Unmeasured**: gfx1013/GFX10.1 itself (see `docs/buffer_bounds.md`), swizzle, unaligned addresses, and the mode 1/2 boundary of `buffer_load_dwordx2..x4` on RDNA2 hardware proper (the gfx1150 proxy shows all dwords in).

Checked by `tests/semantic/test_value_semantics.py` (`RawBufferTailBounds`: the RX 6800 rows, values and the addresses loaded) and the GPU tests `runtime/test/shaders/cs_bounds.asm` (AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT, RX 6800), `cs_buf_tail.asm` (RX 6800, Vulkan, driver 26.11.2; aligned offsets only, since the translator's `Aligned 4` loads at byte-exact addresses were not checked on a Vulkan driver) `cs_oob_select.asm` and `cs_oob_tail.asm`.

`cs_fmt_xy_xyz.asm` shows the whole element deciding for `_xy` and `_xyz` too, measured natively on a Radeon 680M (gfx1035, RDNA2): components that end inside num_records, in an element that doesn't, read 0 and store nothing.
